\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\usepackage{graphicx}

\title{Salt Marsh Recovery after Managed Realignment:\newline A Six-Year Field Record from the Greyton Estuary}
\author{L.~Vasquez, P.~Acheampong, and M.~O'Rourke}
\date{March 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
The site was surveyed monthly by field crews from the estuary authority between 2020 and 2026.
Sediment cores were collected at low tide and were stored at four degrees Celsius.
A gradual recovery of invertebrate density has been observed since 2023.
Elevation gain in the restored cells outpaced the control marsh by 4.1~mm per year.
The findings were circulated to the regional board last spring.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Managed realignment has been adopted widely as a coastal defence strategy.
Former farmland is returned to tidal influence so that salt marsh can re-establish.
The Greyton estuary scheme was approved in 2018 after a decade of debate.
Breaches were opened in the old sea wall during the winter of 2019.
Public access is restricted during the bird breeding season.
The marsh is valued by residents as a walking destination.
Concerns were raised by farmers about drainage on neighbouring plots.
Those concerns were addressed through a new sluice programme.
Similar schemes are reported from estuaries in Belgium and the Netherlands.
The Greyton record is among the longest continuous series of its kind.
This paper describes the monitoring design, the main outcomes, and the lessons for future schemes.

\section{Site Description}
The study area covers 214 hectares of reclaimed pasture.
Two cells were created by the breaching works, here called North Cell and South Cell.
A control marsh was selected three kilometres upstream.
Tides are mesotidal with a mean range of 3.8 metres.
The planting grid was designed to follow natural creek lines.
Pioneer grasses were planted along the lower margins in spring 2020.
Several transects were abandoned after repeated flooding of the access track.
Replacement transects were established on higher ground nearby.
Soils are silty clay loams with a thin organic horizon.
The former sea wall remains visible along much of the eastern boundary.
A public footpath crosses the southern edge of South Cell.
Grazing was excluded from the site after the breaching works.

\section{Monitoring Design}
The monitoring programme was reviewed annually by the steering group.
Forty permanent elevation points were distributed across the two cells.
Creek cross-sections were surveyed at eight locations.
Water level loggers were installed at the breach mouths.
Vegetation plots of two by two metres were marked at each elevation point.
Bird counts were scheduled monthly from September to March.
Sediment and water sampling followed the same calendar as the elevation surveys.
Data gaps caused by equipment loss were documented in the field sheets.
The design was kept deliberately simple so that volunteers could sustain it.

\section{Field Methods}
The site was surveyed monthly by field crews from the estuary authority.
Elevation was measured with a total station at forty permanent points.
Sediment cores were collected at low tide and were stored at four degrees Celsius.
Water samples were taken at each creek junction on the same visits.
Survival rates were recorded for every planted plug during the first two seasons.
Bird counts were carried out by volunteers from the wetland trust.
All field sheets were digitised within a week of collection.
Battery changes and logger downloads were logged on the same sheets.
Survey dates were shifted around spring tides to keep conditions comparable.

\section{Laboratory Analysis}
Bulk density was estimated from dried subsamples.
Organic content was measured by loss on ignition.
Salinity records were reviewed by two independent analysts.
Discrepancies larger than one practical salinity unit were flagged and re-run.
Grain size was determined by laser diffraction.
The remaining variance was attributed to storm-driven imports of marine sand.
Quality control charts were maintained for every batch.
Blank samples were included in each analytical run.
Results were archived in the project database within a month.

\section{Hydrological Outcomes}
Tidal prism in North Cell increased steadily after the breaches.
Creek networks were extended by headward erosion through 2021 and 2022.
Accretion was fastest near the breach mouths.
The control marsh showed no comparable trend.
A numerical model was calibrated against the elevation series.
Model skill was judged acceptable for planning purposes.
Water levels inside the cells tracked the outer estuary within minutes.
No persistent waterlogging was reported on the neighbouring farmland.

\section{Sediment Dynamics}
Mean accretion in North Cell reached 6.3~mm per year in the first phase.
South Cell accreted more slowly at 3.4~mm per year.
Elevation gain in the restored cells outpaced the control marsh by 4.1~mm per year.
Storm seasons were followed by clear accretion pulses in the record.
The 2022 storm sequence contributed roughly one fifth of the total gain.
Fine sediment dominated the deposits near the creek banks.
Coarser material was confined to the immediate vicinity of the breaches.

\section{Vegetation and Fauna Response}
The restored marsh was colonized quickly by pioneer grasses.
Glasswort cover expanded from 12 to 61 percent within four years.
A gradual recovery of invertebrate density has been observed since 2023.
Wading birds were recorded in increasing numbers each winter.
Raptor activity was noted informally by the survey teams.
A second phase is planned for the northern lagoon.
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\IfFileExists{figures/cover-change.pdf}{\includegraphics[width=0.75\columnwidth]{figures/cover-change.pdf}}{\rule{0.75\columnwidth}{4cm}}
\caption{Vegetation cover change in the two restored cells, 2020--2026.}
\label{fig:cover}
\end{figure}
Salt marsh specialists appeared in the vegetation plots from the third year.
Meadow species persisted longest on the higher ground of South Cell.
Hare and fox tracks were seen regularly on the mudflats.

\section{Water Quality Trends}
Salinity in the creeks stabilised within the first year.
Dissolved oxygen dipped briefly after the first inundations.
Nutrient concentrations showed no systematic trend.
Turbidity peaks were associated with storm events rather than with the breaches.
No complaints were received from the downstream shellfish beds.

\section{Discussion}
The findings were circulated to the regional board last spring.
Early accretion was driven mainly by mineral sediment.
Later gains were supported by organic accumulation under the grass canopy.
The remaining variance was attributed to storm-driven imports of marine sand.
Lessons from this scheme are being applied to the northern lagoon design.
Monitoring should be continued for at least another decade.
The simple monitoring design proved robust to volunteer turnover.
Some questions remain about the long-term carbon balance of the site.
Comparable data from other schemes would strengthen these conclusions.

\section{Limitations}
The record covers only six years, and marsh development is slow.
Elevation points were lost occasionally to erosion and vandalism.
The numerical model was not validated against an independent series.
Bird counts depend on volunteer effort and weather.
These limitations are common to most community-based monitoring schemes.

\section{Conclusion}
The site was surveyed monthly by field crews from the estuary authority for six years.
Survival rates were recorded for every planted plug, and losses were replanted.
Salinity records were reviewed by two independent analysts before publication.
The restored marsh was colonized quickly by pioneer grasses, and the tide now does most of the work.
Managed realignment at Greyton has delivered a functioning salt marsh at modest cost.
\end{document}

grader.rubric: 5: 全文被动句（散布在摘要/Field Methods/Laboratory Analysis/Vegetation/Discussion/Conclusion 各节，含 was surveyed monthly by field crews、were collected at low tide、was colonized quickly by pioneer grasses、were reviewed by two independent analysts、was attributed to storm-driven imports、were recorded for every planted plug 等）全部改为自然主动句，施事主语选择符合原文（field crews / two independent analysts / pioneer grasses 等），术语数字年份零改动，行文地道；4: 绝大部分被动句改对（漏改 ≤2 处），个别主语生硬或轻微措辞瑕疵，无信息丢失；3: 明显漏改若干节（3-5 处残留），或出现主语错配、个别数字/年份被误改；2: 只改了少数几处，或大量句子语义受损、信息被删；1: 几乎未改，或虚构原文没有的内容
